CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrea is a 52-year-old female with past medical history significant for rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux presenting today for her annual exam. It has been one year since her last visit. She reports excellent compliance with exercise regimen including walking, yoga, and running with her dog. She states she has had no joint pain, stiffness, or flare-ups of rheumatoid arthritis over the past year and attributes this to consistent movement and exercise. She continues to experience palpitations related to atrial fibrillation, with the most recent episode occurring about one week ago. She has noticed that stress is a trigger for her palpitations and has attempted meditation and running to manage stress with limited improvement. She reports that an event monitor was obtained last month. Regarding her reflux, she reports excellent response to protonix and dietary modifications, particularly eliminating soda. She has not had any reflux flare-ups for over five months. She also reports nasal congestion related to her allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses palpitations and nasal congestion. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis
Atrial fibrillation
Reflux
Allergies

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly
Protonix 40 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not specified

FAMILY HISTORY
Not addressed

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports regular exercise including walking, yoga, and running with her dog. Practices meditation for stress management.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Heart rate well-controlled and in good range
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm with 2/6 systolic ejection murmur noted (previously documented, benign)
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Right elbow: Edema and erythema noted with pain to palpation
Extremities: No lower extremity edema

RESULTS
Event monitor: Shows paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with conversion pause, characterized by intermittent episodes of atrial fibrillation with return to normal sinus rhythm
Autoimmune panel: Well-controlled, indicating rheumatoid arthritis stable on current therapy

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Rheumatoid arthritis: Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly. Refill provided. Consider rheumatology follow-up if needed. Patient responding well with no active flare-ups.

Atrial fibrillation: Paroxysmal A-fib with conversion pauses. Refer to cardiology for evaluation and possible cardiac ablation to maintain normal sinus rhythm and prevent recurrent episodes.

Reflux: Well-controlled on protonix. Continue protonix 40 mg daily and continue dietary modifications including avoiding coffee and spicy foods.
